text.p: Barry's Jewellers Inc., the nation's fifth-largest retailer of fine jewelry, said Monday it has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection and closed about 34 unprofitable or under-performing stores.

The company said it made the filing in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Los Angeles on Sunday to ensure a continued flow of merchandise to its stores and to allow the implementation of planned capital restructuring initiatives.
Barry's, whose stores are mainly in malls, said it expects to obtain enough inventory in anticipation of the Christmas holiday season.
"By taking action prior to the start of the holiday buying season, we will assure the continued flow of merchandise to our stores," said Sam Merksamer, chief executive.

Since he joined the Monrovia, Calif.-based company in February, Merksamer has installed an entirely new management team of 18 operations and marketing executives from leading jewelry chains and other major retailers.
Merksamer led Merksamer Jewellers, Inc., a national retail jewelry store chain, through a successful Chapter 11 proceeding in 1992. He sold the company in 1996 to a major Pacific Northwest retailer.

Barry's, which traces its roots to 1891, operates 130 retail jewelry stores, mainly in California, Texas, Arizona, Utah, Colorado, Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, Montana, North Carolina and South Carolina. It has about 1,000 employees at its stores.
Barry's stock closed Friday at 34.4 cents on Nasdaq.
